title: LLM Safety and Application Design
description: Assess risks and build human-centered language-model applications.

questions.prompt: What should a safe refusal do when a request falls outside permitted use?
options: Briefly explain the boundary and, when possible, offer a safe alternative
Provide the disallowed instructions indirectly
Claim the system has no limitations
Reveal hidden policy text
questions.explanation: A useful refusal communicates the limit without enabling the harmful request and can redirect to benign help.

questions.prompt: A content filter alone can guarantee that an LLM application will never produce harmful output.
questions.explanation: Filters can miss context or be bypassed; safety needs layered prevention, testing, monitoring, and response.

questions.prompt: Which are useful elements of LLM red-team testing?
options: Probe adversarial prompts
Test tool-use boundaries
Include multiple languages and user contexts
Test only the default happy path
questions.explanation: Adversarial and context-diverse testing can uncover risks missed by ordinary expected-use tests.

questions.prompt: When should an LLM workflow offer human escalation?
options: When uncertainty or impact exceeds its validated scope
Only when the user asks for a longer answer
Whenever the model uses punctuation
Never if responses are streamed
questions.explanation: Escalation is important when consequences or uncertainty exceed what the system is validated to handle.

questions.prompt: What is a prudent principle for LLMs in high-impact decisions?
options: Keep qualified human accountability and meaningful review
Let the model decide solely from a confidence score
Avoid documenting limitations
Use an untested prompt for speed
questions.explanation: High-impact settings need accountable human processes, appeal mechanisms, and validated evidence.

questions.prompt: Which controls can reduce privacy risk in an LLM application?
options: Minimize personal data sent to the model
Redact sensitive fields when feasible
Define retention and access controls
Log every raw prompt forever
questions.explanation: Minimization, redaction, and retention controls limit exposure; indefinite raw logging is risky.

questions.prompt: An LLM can be assumed never to reproduce personal information from its training data.
questions.explanation: Models can memorize or reproduce data in some conditions, so privacy risk and output handling require assessment.

questions.prompt: Why track provenance for documents used in an LLM knowledge base?
options: Understand rights, source quality, and update history
Guarantee generated text has no overlap
Remove the need for review
Increase the model context limit
questions.explanation: Provenance supports rights management, source auditing, and freshness checks.

questions.prompt: What is a critical access-control concern in multi-user retrieval systems?
options: A query must retrieve only documents the caller is allowed to see
All indexed documents should be public
The model’s answer is an authorization token
Filtering after generation is always sufficient
questions.explanation: Authorization should constrain retrieval itself; revealing restricted context before filtering can leak information.

questions.prompt: Which steps can help examine demographic performance disparities?
options: Use appropriate and lawfully handled subgroup data
Compare error patterns across affected groups
Engage domain experts and affected stakeholders
Assume one overall average is enough
questions.explanation: Subgroup evaluation and stakeholder input can expose differences hidden by aggregate metrics.

questions.prompt: Which interface choice can reduce overreliance on model output?
options: Show uncertainty and source limitations clearly
Present every answer as authoritative
Hide provenance and alternatives
Remove user correction mechanisms
questions.explanation: Clear limits, evidence, and correction paths help users judge outputs rather than defer blindly.

questions.prompt: Users may benefit from knowing when content or decisions are generated with AI.
questions.explanation: Disclosure supports informed use, especially where synthetic content or automated assistance could be consequential.

questions.prompt: How should an LLM feature be evaluated for accessibility?
options: Test with assistive technologies and users with diverse needs
Assume language generation is inherently accessible
Use only the development team’s devices
Remove alternative interaction paths
questions.explanation: Accessibility requires testing real interactions and ensuring alternatives for diverse users.

questions.prompt: What should an LLM incident log aim to capture while respecting privacy?
options: Relevant model and prompt-template versions
Tool actions and outcomes
A minimal, access-controlled record for investigation
Every secret and raw personal field indefinitely
questions.explanation: Useful, minimized, protected records support response without unnecessary sensitive-data retention.

questions.prompt: Why assess third-party model and component supply chains?
options: Updates or dependencies can change security, behavior, and licensing
Third-party models cannot have vulnerabilities
It guarantees model accuracy
It replaces access controls
questions.explanation: Model providers, packages, and updates bring operational, security, and legal dependencies to manage.

questions.prompt: Passing a small set of jailbreak tests proves that a model is resistant to all prompt attacks.
questions.explanation: Attack strategies evolve, so no finite test set proves universal resistance.

questions.prompt: What is a responsible way to communicate model uncertainty?
options: Describe what is unknown and suggest verification for consequential claims
Use a precise percentage without calibration evidence
Remove caveats to sound confident
Claim uncertainty means the answer is false
questions.explanation: Useful uncertainty language is calibrated to evidence and helps users verify important claims.

questions.prompt: When updating an LLM-powered product, which changes merit reevaluation?
options: Switching model versions
Changing system prompts or tools
Changing retrieval sources
Changing a button’s border color only
questions.explanation: Model, prompt, tool, and corpus changes can alter behavior and should trigger relevant regression checks.

questions.prompt: How should user feedback about LLM errors be used?
options: Review and categorize it to improve safeguards and product quality
Automatically treat each report as verified ground truth
Publish identifying details by default
Ignore reports that disagree with benchmarks
questions.explanation: Feedback can reveal real-world failures but needs triage, privacy protection, and verification.

questions.prompt: What is the best approach when a model output is outside the product’s validated scope?
options: Decline or route to a suitable process rather than imply reliability
Present it as guaranteed because the model responded
Hide the scope statement
Increase output length
questions.explanation: Applications should enforce intended-use boundaries and avoid presenting unsupported outputs as reliable.
